answer_1.quote: We conduct our experiments on three widelyused datasets: AlpacaEval , WMT19 (de-en) (Foundation, 2019) and TruthfulQA . Following prior work on multi-objective alignment , we evaluate helpfulness on Al-pacaEval and WMT19 (de-en), and truthfulness on TruthfulQA.
answer_1.outputs: responses to instructions and translations from German to English

answer_2.quote: Recent work adopts metrics based on w A to quantify self-preference bias . However, this approach conflates the quality of the responses with the selfpreference bias of the judge model , leading to biased estimations.

answer_3.quote: LLMs as judges is proposed as a valuable complement to both rule-based and human-based evaluation approaches . By leveraging their extensive world knowledge and reasoning abilities, LLMs show a high degree of alignment with human judgments and offer a convenient, cost-effective al-ternative to human-based evaluation .

answer_4.quote: To validate the reliability of the gold judgments, we compare it with actual human annotations. Specifically, we randomly sample 100 instructions from AlpacaEval and obtain the corresponding responses from three different model pairs. Human annotators are then instructed to compare the responses generated by the two models in each pair and determine which one is more helpful.
